title: Power Earnings Gap
teaches: The Power Earnings Gap as we trade it: an established leader in a base or a quiet uptrend reports a quarter the market did not expect and gaps up on heavy volume; the gap day closes strong with the gap still open; we buy as price trades over the first orderly pause high with a market order, the stop sits a few cents under the pause or trigger-day low, a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the 10-day or 21-day trail, and a loss taken at the stop is the system working.

questions.q: In one line, what is a Power Earnings Gap?
choices: An earnings gap with a strong close
A gap on a news headline, no report
A gap that fills by the close
A slow drift above the 200-day
questions.answer: An earnings gap with a strong close
questions.why: An earnings gap with a strong close. Stewie: a stock that gaps up after reporting strong earnings and closes the day by printing a very strong candle.
questions.lesson_line: A PEG is an earnings gap that closes strong.

wrong.A gap on a news headline, no report: It needs a report. A headline gap with no report belongs to the News Gapper.
wrong.A gap that fills by the close: A gap that fills is the opposite of a strong close; the setup is off.
wrong.A slow drift above the 200-day: A PEG is a gap day, not a drift.

questions.q: The PEG day is the first regular session after the earnings report.
questions.why: True. It is the report day for a report before the open, and the next session for a report after the close.
questions.lesson_line: Find the report time first. That tells you which session is the PEG day.

questions.q: Which earnings gap day is not a Power Earnings Gap?
choices: It opens up, fades, and closes red
It opens up and closes near the high
It opens up, dips, closes strong
It opens up and rallies all day
questions.answer: It opens up, fades, and closes red
questions.why: It opens up, fades, and closes red. Stewie: a gap that reverses and closes in the red is not what he wants to see in a PEG candidate.
questions.lesson_line: A gap that fades into a red close is not a PEG.

wrong.It opens up and closes near the high: That is the ideal PEG candle.
wrong.It opens up, dips, closes strong: A dip that recovers into a strong close is still a PEG day.
wrong.It opens up and rallies all day: A day that rallies all day closes strong, the ideal candle.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: On a PEG pause buy, the stop goes a few ___ under the pause low or the trigger day's low.
questions.why: Cents. The stop sits a few cents under the pause low or the trigger day's low, not exactly on it.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the low.

questions.q: Stewie starts his gap-and-go in the after-hours session. We buy PEGs the same way.
questions.why: False. We buy at market in regular hours only. No pre-market and no after-hours buys, unlike Stewie's gap-and-go.
questions.lesson_line: Regular hours only. The gap-and-go is not ours.

questions.q: Which market readings do we want for a PEG?
choices: Green or Yellow
Orange or Red
Red only
Any; earnings ignore the market
questions.why: Green or Yellow. Orange allows A+ setups only, and Red is mostly cash and shorts.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market first: Green or Yellow for PEGs.

wrong.Orange or Red: Orange is for A+ setups only, and Red is mostly cash.
wrong.Red only: Red means mostly cash and shorts, not new longs.
wrong.Any; earnings ignore the market: Earnings season does not switch the market reading off.

questions.q: Stewie calls a close at or near the highs of the session the ideal PEG candle.
questions.why: True. Stewie: a candle that closes at or near the highs is the most ideal Power Earnings Gap candidate. Our A grade is a close in the top quarter.
questions.lesson_line: The close matters as much as the gap.

questions.q: Where does an A-grade PEG day close?
choices: In the top quarter of its range
Anywhere above the open
Just above the prior close
Mid-range on heavy volume
questions.answer: In the top quarter of its range
questions.why: In the top quarter of its range. A close at or near the high is the ideal candle.
questions.lesson_line: A close near the high is the A grade.

wrong.Anywhere above the open: Above the open is not enough for the A grade.
wrong.Just above the prior close: A close that low has given most of the gap back.
wrong.Mid-range on heavy volume: Heavy volume does not fix a mid-range close.

questions.q: A slight undercut of the PEG-day low that closes back over it kills the PEG.
questions.why: False. A slight undercut that closes back over the PEG-day low is not an invalidation. The later test of the gap-up low is Gap Support.
questions.lesson_line: A slight undercut that reclaims is not a failure.

questions.q: Before you buy, which event ends the PEG setup?
choices: A daily close under the PEG-day low
A quiet day on lighter volume
A pullback to the 10-day
An inside day in the pause
questions.answer: A daily close under the PEG-day low
questions.why: A daily close under the PEG-day low. The gap-day low has given way on a close, so there is nothing to buy.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the PEG-day low ends it.

wrong.A quiet day on lighter volume: Quiet days on lighter volume are what a good pause looks like.
wrong.A pullback to the 10-day: A shallow pullback that holds the PEG-day low is still a pause.
wrong.An inside day in the pause: An inside day is one of the tight pauses we look for.

questions.q: Before a buy, a trade back to the prior close means the gap filled and the PEG is off.
questions.why: True. A trade at or under the prior close is a filled gap. Morpheus: any stock that fills the opening gap should be avoided.
questions.lesson_line: A filled gap is a dead PEG.

questions.q: Which stock passes our liquidity rule?
choices: $25 and $50 million a day
$8 and $60 million a day
$40 and $12 million a day
$6 and $5 million a day
questions.why: $25 and $50 million a day. We trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day.
questions.lesson_line: Ten dollars and twenty million a day, or we skip.

wrong.$40 and $12 million a day: The dollar volume is under $20 million a day.
wrong.$6 and $5 million a day: Both fail: price under $10 and volume under $20 million.

questions.q: Which session is the PEG day?
questions.story: A company reports after the close on Tuesday. You check the earnings calendar that evening.
choices: Wednesday, the next session
Tuesday, the report day
Thursday, after it settles
Friday, as the pause forms
questions.why: Wednesday. A report after the close belongs to the next regular session. The report day is the PEG day only for a report before the open.
questions.lesson_line: After the close, the next session is the PEG day.

wrong.Tuesday, the report day: Tuesday's regular session was over before the report.
wrong.Thursday, after it settles: Waiting a day misses the reaction; the first session is the PEG day.
wrong.Friday, as the pause forms: The pause comes after the PEG day, not before.

questions.q: Growing sales and earnings, a beat and a raise make a PEG stronger, but the chart still comes first.
questions.why: True. Growing sales and earnings, a beat and ideally a raise are a grade cue, not a gate. The chart comes first.
questions.lesson_line: Fundamentals are a cue. The chart decides.

questions.q: On a PEG you may add shares later if volume climbs after the buy.
questions.why: False. One buy at one price with one stop. No adding when volume comes in and no starter position.
questions.lesson_line: One buy, one price, one stop. No adding.

questions.q: Bought at 48.93 with the stop at 48.20. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 51.12. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. BIDU ran 27.7R in our scan.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: The PEG day's low is 70.00, high 76.00, close 74.80. Where in the range did it close, from 0 to 1?
questions.why: 0.8. The close minus the low, divided by the high minus the low. That is the top quarter of the range, the A-grade close.
questions.lesson_line: Close minus low, over the range. Top quarter is the A grade.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on a PEG pause buy?
choices: A few cents under the pause low
At the prior close, the gap-fill price
Exactly on the PEG-day low
A fixed 5% under the fill
questions.answer: A few cents under the pause low
questions.why: A few cents under the pause low or the trigger day's low, whichever the plan names. It is never wider than under the PEG-day low.
questions.lesson_line: A few cents under a real low, never wider than the gap-day low.

wrong.At the prior close, the gap-fill price: The prior close is far below the pause. That is a much wider stop than the rule allows.
wrong.Exactly on the PEG-day low: The PEG-day low is the outer limit, and the stop sits a few cents under a low, not on it.
wrong.A fixed 5% under the fill: A fixed percentage ignores the chart. The stop sits under a real low.

questions.q: A PEG in profit can be held through its next earnings report whatever the open gain.
questions.why: False. Sell before the next report unless the trade is up 5R. Hold through a report only at 5R or better.
questions.lesson_line: Into the next report only with 5R in hand.

questions.q: Which of the two can you take?
questions.story: The market reading turns Orange. One PEG has a loose pause that undercuts the PEG-day low. Another has a tight pause on lighter volume holding the PEG-day close.
choices: Only the A+ one
Both, at half size
Neither; Orange means all cash
Both, with a wider stop
questions.why: Only the A+ one. In an Orange market we take A+ setups only. A tight pause holding the PEG-day close is an A+ cue.
questions.lesson_line: Orange: A+ setups only.

wrong.Both, at half size: Orange allows A+ setups at their size, not B setups at half.
wrong.Neither; Orange means all cash: Orange still allows an A+ setup.
wrong.Both, with a wider stop: A wider stop breaks the stop rule and the size formula.

questions.q: How do we trail the last third of a PEG?
choices: A close under the 10- or 21-day
Sell on a touch of the 50-day
Hold to the next earnings report
Sell at 10R, whatever the chart
questions.why: Sell on a close under the 10-day for a fast mover or the 21-day for a steadier one. That is the default trail.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the last third under the 10- or 21-day.

wrong.Sell on a touch of the 50-day: The 50-day is far below a fast trend. The default trail is the 10- or 21-day.
wrong.Hold to the next earnings report: Holding into the next report needs 5R and is not the trail.
wrong.Sell at 10R, whatever the chart: A fixed R target is not the trail; the average decides.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: At 3R we sell a ___ of the position.
questions.why: Third. The hard rule for the first trim is a third at 3R. Another third comes off at 5R.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R.

questions.q: Prior close 50.00, today's open 55.60. How big is the gap, in percent?
questions.why: 11.2. The open minus the prior close, divided by the prior close. A gap of 10% or more is an A-grade cue.
questions.lesson_line: Gap percent is open over prior close. Ten percent is an A cue.

questions.q: Which trade is this?
questions.story: Three weeks after a PEG, the stock dips under the PEG-day low and closes back over it.
choices: Gap Support, the later test
A new PEG; buy it
A failed PEG; short it
A News Gapper
questions.why: Gap Support. A slight undercut of the gap-day low that closes back over it is not a PEG failure. The gap day is the PEG; the later test is Gap Support.
questions.lesson_line: The gap day is a PEG. The later test of its low is Gap Support.

wrong.A new PEG; buy it: A PEG is the report's reaction day and its first pause, not a test weeks later.
wrong.A failed PEG; short it: A close back over the low is not a failure, and we do not short a PEG.
wrong.A News Gapper: A News Gapper needs a headline that is not a report; this gap was earnings.

questions.q: Fill 90.25, stop 88.19. How far is the stop from the fill, in percent?
questions.why: 2.3. The fill minus the stop, divided by the fill. That sits inside the usual 3%. LULU had these levels.
questions.lesson_line: Stop distance is the fill minus the stop, over the fill.

questions.q: Buy or pass?
questions.story: The pause high is 60.00. You were in a meeting, and at 10:15 the stock trades 62.80.
choices: Pass, over 4% past the trigger
Buy, the breakout is confirmed
Buy half size to limit the risk
Buy it with a wider stop to fit
questions.why: Pass. 62.80 is more than 4% over the 60.00 trigger. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays put and the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Miss it rather than chase it. Four percent and done.

wrong.Buy, the breakout is confirmed: Confirmed and too far away are both true. The chase line is 4%.
wrong.Buy half size to limit the risk: Half of a bad entry is still a bad entry.
wrong.Buy it with a wider stop to fit: A wider stop to fit a late entry is the mistake, not the fix.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: A leader reports after the close and is up 12% in after-hours trading on huge volume. A chat room says to buy now.
choices: Wait for regular hours and the pause
Buy now with a limit order
Buy half now, half at the open
Buy now; it will gap higher
questions.answer: Wait for regular hours and the pause
questions.why: Wait. We never buy outside regular hours. The PEG day is the next regular session, and the buy comes later, off the pause.
questions.lesson_line: No after-hours buys. Wait for the regular session.

wrong.Buy now with a limit order: Entries are market orders in regular hours, not after-hours limits.
wrong.Buy half now, half at the open: Half an after-hours buy is still an after-hours buy.
wrong.Buy now; it will gap higher: A gap that is going higher can wait for the regular session.

questions.q: What is the setup now?
questions.story: Four days after the gap, the stock closes under the PEG-day low. You have not bought yet.
choices: Off; no PEG buy
A deeper pause; keep waiting
On; the gap has not filled
A Gap Support; buy the close
questions.why: Off. A daily close under the PEG-day low before a buy ends the PEG. The gap-day low has given way on a close.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the gap-day low means no PEG.

wrong.A deeper pause; keep waiting: The low gave way on a close. More waiting does not undo that.
wrong.On; the gap has not filled: Not filling is not enough; the low gave way on a close.
wrong.A Gap Support; buy the close: Gap Support needs a close back over the line, not a close under it.

questions.q: Where is the stop now?
questions.story: You bought at 30.00 with the stop at 29.40. A follow-up headline gaps it open at 29.10. The first 30-minute bar's low is 28.95.
choices: 28.95, the first 30-minute low
29.10, sell at the open
29.40, wait for a reclaim
28.80, two R under the fill
questions.why: 28.95. On a gap through the stop, the first 30-minute low is the new stop. You are out only if that is past 2R, and it is not.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop: the first 30-minute low decides.

wrong.29.10, sell at the open: The first 30-minute bar decides; it is not an automatic sale at the open.
wrong.29.40, wait for a reclaim: The old stop is gone once the gap trades through it.
wrong.28.80, two R under the fill: Two R is the ceiling, not a stop to place.

questions.q: On a PEG the stop moves to breakeven as soon as the buy fills.
questions.why: False. The stop moves to breakeven between 2R and 5R, and by default at the first trim.
questions.lesson_line: First trim, then the stop to breakeven.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: A PEG closed strong on Thursday. Three quiet days since have held above the PEG-day low. This morning the stock trades over the highest high of those three days.
choices: Buy at market; stop under the low
Wait for the close to confirm
Buy at the PEG-day high with a limit
Skip it; the gap is old
questions.answer: Buy at market; stop under the low
questions.why: Buy at market. The trigger is a market buy as price trades over the pause high, with the stop a few cents under the low.
questions.lesson_line: Buy as price trades over the pause high.

wrong.Wait for the close to confirm: Waiting for the close hands away the trigger and the price.
wrong.Buy at the PEG-day high with a limit: A limit at the PEG-day high is not the trigger; the pause high is.
wrong.Skip it; the gap is old: The gap is still open and the low is holding; nothing says skip.

questions.q: PEG or News Gapper?
questions.story: A stock gaps 6.3% on 2.7x volume and closes at 96% of its range. The earnings calendar shows no report that day. The last one was five weeks ago.
choices: News Gapper; not a report day
PEG; the gap and close qualify
Episodic Pivot; any gap with volume
Kicker; it closed at the high
questions.answer: News Gapper; not a report day
questions.why: News Gapper. A PEG day is a report's reaction day. This gap came on a headline that was not a report, so it belongs to the News Gapper lesson.
questions.lesson_line: Check the earnings calendar. No report, no PEG.

wrong.PEG; the gap and close qualify: The close and volume are fine. The catalyst is what fails.
wrong.Episodic Pivot; any gap with volume: An Episodic Pivot needs a neglected name and a named surprise, not just volume.
wrong.Kicker; it closed at the high: A Kicker needs a weak red close the day before.

questions.q: PEG or High Volume Edge?
questions.story: A well-known company reports and gaps up strongly. It trades its biggest volume in a year, 7.6x its average, and closes strong.
choices: A PEG; earnings on a known name
A High Volume Edge; a record
Both; the gap and volume stack
Neither; 7.6x is far too heavy
questions.answer: A PEG; earnings on a known name
questions.why: A PEG. An earnings spike on an established name stays a PEG even at a one-year volume record. ASML at 7.6x was still just a PEG.
questions.lesson_line: Earnings on a known name stays a PEG, even on record volume.

wrong.A High Volume Edge; a record: An HVE dwarfs every prior day, usually on a lesser-known name.
wrong.Both; the gap and volume stack: It is one setup. The catalyst and the name decide which.
wrong.Neither; 7.6x is far too heavy: Heavy volume is a cue here, not a disqualifier.

questions.q: PEG or Kicker?
questions.story: Monday ends with a weak red close. Tuesday opens 2% higher with no earnings and no headline, on light volume.
choices: A Kicker; weak red close, small gap
A PEG; any gap up counts
A News Gapper; any gap is news
An Episodic Pivot; the close was weak
questions.answer: A Kicker; weak red close, small gap
questions.why: A Kicker. It needs a weak red close and a small gap on positioning, rarely earnings. A PEG is an earnings reaction day.
questions.lesson_line: A weak red close, then a small gap on no news, is a Kicker.

wrong.A PEG; any gap up counts: A PEG needs a report; this gap had no earnings.
wrong.A News Gapper; any gap is news: A News Gapper needs a named catalyst, and there is none.
wrong.An Episodic Pivot; the close was weak: An Episodic Pivot needs a named surprise and a neglected name.

questions.q: PEG or Episodic Pivot?
questions.story: A stock nobody follows is down 20% over six months. It reports and gaps 15% on 5x volume.
choices: An Episodic Pivot; a neglected name
A PEG; any earnings gap is one
A PEG; 15% is a big gap
Neither; it was falling
questions.answer: An Episodic Pivot; a neglected name
questions.why: An Episodic Pivot. A PEG is an established leader in a base or a quiet uptrend. An EP is a neglected name, flat or down for six months.
questions.lesson_line: Look at the six months before the report.

wrong.A PEG; any earnings gap is one: A PEG comes from an established leader, not a forgotten name.
wrong.A PEG; 15% is a big gap: Size does not decide it. The months before the report do.
wrong.Neither; it was falling: A neglected name re-priced by a surprise is exactly an EP.

questions.q: Grade the two.
questions.story: Two earnings gaps of about 10% on 4x volume, both closing at the high. One comes out of a five-month base. The other follows a 45% run in three months.
choices: First stronger; second a B-
Both A+; the gap day is the same
Second stronger; strength builds
Both B-; 10% is small
questions.why: First stronger, second a B-. For an A, the stock is not up more than 30% in the 65 sessions before the gap. A late gap after a big run is a B-.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet before the gap is an A cue. A late gap is a B-.

wrong.Both A+; the gap day is the same: The days look alike, but the months before them do not.
wrong.Second stronger; strength builds: A big run into the report is the late-gap warning, not a plus.
wrong.Both B-; 10% is small: A gap of 10% or more is an A cue, not a small one.

questions.q: Grade each pause.
questions.story: Two pauses follow the same kind of gap. One is three tight days on lighter volume that hold the PEG-day close. The other is seven loose days that dip under the PEG-day low before closing back over it.
choices: First an A+ cue; second a B-
Both the same; the gap decides
First a B-; tight is too slow
Both A; a pause is a pause
questions.answer: First an A+ cue; second a B-
questions.why: First an A+ cue, second a B-. A tight pause on lighter volume that holds the PEG-day close is an A+ cue. A loose, deep pause that undercuts the low is a B-.
questions.lesson_line: Tight and holding is A+. Loose and deep is a B-.

wrong.Both the same; the gap decides: The pause is half of the trade, and these two are very different.
wrong.First a B-; tight is too slow: Tight days that hold the close are the best pause, not a slow one.
wrong.Both A; a pause is a pause: A deep undercut is a weaker pause, not an equal one.

questions.q: A PEG still under 1R after 10 trading days is held while the stop has not been hit.
questions.why: False. Time stop: still under 1R after 10 trading days, sell, even if the stop has not been hit. It frees the money for a better trade.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days under 1R and we sell.

questions.q: When do you sell the first third?
questions.story: You bought at 40.00 with the stop at 39.00, so 3R is 43.00. This morning the stock opens at 43.60.
choices: At the open, 43.60
At 43.00 with a limit order
At the close, after a look
Not until 5R
questions.why: At the open. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open, not waited on.
questions.lesson_line: A trim level passed at the open is taken at the open.

wrong.At 43.00 with a limit order: The stock is already past 43.00; a limit there sits under the market.
wrong.At the close, after a look: Waiting hands back what the open gave you.
wrong.Not until 5R: The first third comes off at 3R, and the price is already past it.

questions.q: Account 50,000. Risk 0.5%. Fill 90.25, stop 88.19. How many shares?
questions.why: 121. Account times risk percent, divided by the fill minus the stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: The pause high is 61.00 and the pause low is 57.90. The honest stop is 5.2% from the fill. A friend says to put the stop at 59.50 so the size looks normal.
choices: Size down by formula, or skip
Put the stop at 59.50 to fit
Buy full size anyway, same stop
Put the stop at the prior close
questions.answer: Size down by formula, or skip
questions.why: Size down by the formula, or skip. The honest stop stays where the chart puts it. Pulling it in is never the fix.
questions.lesson_line: If the honest stop does not fit, size down or skip.

wrong.Put the stop at 59.50 to fit: Pulling the stop in to fit the size is the mistake, not the plan.
wrong.Buy full size anyway, same stop: Full size on a stop that wide breaks the risk rule.
wrong.Put the stop at the prior close: The prior close is an even wider stop and ignores the chart.

questions.q: Hold or sell?
questions.story: You are up 3.5R on a PEG. The next report is in two sessions.
choices: Sell before the report; not up 5R
Hold; the last report was a winner
Hold half, sell half
Hold; the stop protects you
questions.answer: Sell before the report; not up 5R
questions.why: Sell before the report. A PEG is held through the next report only when it is up 5R. Up 3.5R is not enough.
questions.lesson_line: Under 5R going into a report, sell first.

wrong.Hold; the last report was a winner: The last report says nothing about the next one.
wrong.Hold half, sell half: A half position under 5R still carries the report risk.
wrong.Hold; the stop protects you: A stop does not protect against a gap through it.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought a PEG pause break. Ten trading days later it sits at 0.4R, never near 3R and never near the stop.
choices: Sell; under 1R after 10 sessions
Hold; the stop has not been hit yet
Add; it is coiling for a move
Move the stop to breakeven and wait
questions.why: Sell. Under 1R after 10 trading days is the time stop. The stop is not hit, but the trade has not earned its place.
questions.lesson_line: A slow PEG under 1R gets sold on day ten.

wrong.Hold; the stop has not been hit yet: The time stop exists for exactly this trade.
wrong.Add; it is coiling for a move: Adding breaks one buy, one price, one stop.
wrong.Move the stop to breakeven and wait: Breakeven comes at the first trim, not as a way to wait.

questions.q: How do you start?
questions.story: A correction just ended and the market reading turned Green. It is earnings season, and six leaders gapped on reports this week.
choices: A few positions; add as they work
All six; Green is full risk
None; wait for a second Green week
One; earnings gaps are risky now
questions.answer: A few positions; add as they work
questions.why: A few positions, adding more as the first ones work. After a correction, start small and add as they work. The first earnings season after a correction is one this setup favors.
questions.lesson_line: After a correction, start small and add as they work.

wrong.All six; Green is full risk: Start with a few and add only as the first ones work.
wrong.None; wait for a second Green week: Waiting gives up the first earnings season after a correction, which this setup favors.
wrong.One; earnings gaps are risky now: That season is one this setup favors; start with a few and add as they work.

questions.q: Take the pause break?
questions.story: A $24 stock trades about $12 million a day. It gaps 14% on earnings on 6x volume, closes at the high, and sets up a perfect pause.
choices: No; under $20 million a day
Yes; the gap day's volume is huge
Yes, at half size
Yes; $24 is a fine price
questions.why: No. The price passes, but a stock that trades $12 million a day fails the $20 million floor. A great gap does not change the liquidity rule.
questions.lesson_line: Liquidity first: $10 and $20 million a day.

wrong.Yes; the gap day's volume is huge: The rule is about the usual dollar volume, not one big day.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not fix a liquidity failure.
wrong.Yes; $24 is a fine price: The price passes, but the dollar volume fails.

questions.q: The PEG comes in about four earnings-season windows a year, so we keep a PEG list each quarter.
questions.why: True. The setup comes in four windows a year, so we keep a PEG list each quarter and watch the reports.
questions.lesson_line: Four seasons a year. Keep a PEG list each quarter.

questions.q: The stock's average daily volume is 400,000 shares. What is the most you should own?
questions.why: 4,000. We never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume. One percent of 400,000 is the cap.
questions.lesson_line: Never more than one percent of a day's average volume.

questions.q: What did that loss pay for?
questions.story: NVDA, 2024. A PEG gapped 11.2% on 1.9x volume and closed at 0.99 of its range, after a 36% run in 65 sessions. You bought the pause break and the stop went that week.
choices: A late gap after a big run
A report with no beat
A buy made after hours
A stop set too wide
questions.answer: A late gap after a big run
questions.why: A late gap after a big run. The 36% run before the report was past the 30% A-grade cue. The loss was a planned one-R loss.
questions.lesson_line: A big run into the report is a warning even on a perfect gap.

wrong.A report with no beat: Nothing in the story says the report missed.
wrong.A buy made after hours: The buy came on a gap open in regular hours.
wrong.A stop set too wide: The stop was only 0.5% away, which is tight, not wide.

questions.q: What was that loss?
questions.story: CELH, 2023. A 10.6% earnings gap on 7.5x volume closed at 0.61. After a seven-day pause, you bought the break at 45.07 with a 2.9% stop. It went straight to the stop.
choices: A planned loss on a weaker setup
A mistake; the stop was too tight
A mistake; the volume was too heavy
Bad luck; nothing in the chart
questions.answer: A planned loss on a weaker setup
questions.why: A planned loss on a weaker setup. The close was only just strong and the pause was already a drift when it triggered. The stop did its job.
questions.lesson_line: A weak close and a drifting pause make a weaker trade. The stop paid for it.

wrong.A mistake; the stop was too tight: A 2.9% stop is inside the usual 3%. It was not too tight.
wrong.A mistake; the volume was too heavy: Heavy volume is a plus on a PEG, not a flaw.
wrong.Bad luck; nothing in the chart: The chart gave warnings: a weak close and a drifting pause.

questions.q: Was that a mistake?
questions.story: ELF, 2023. A 10.7% gap on 4.6x volume, close at 0.98, then a clean pause. You bought the eighth-day break at 107.16 with a stop 2.6% away. It never reached 1R and the stop traded.
choices: No; a planned loss, sized by the stop
Yes; you should have skipped the PEG
Yes; widen the stop next time
Yes; you should have bought day one
questions.answer: No; a planned loss, sized by the stop
questions.why: No. A textbook gap and a textbook pause still lost. The plan sizes by the stop so a loss at the stop is about 1R and the system keeps working.
questions.lesson_line: Every gate can pass and the stop can still go.

wrong.Yes; you should have skipped the PEG: Every test passed. Skipping a clean setup is not a plan.
wrong.Yes; widen the stop next time: The stop only moves up. Widening it breaks the rule.
wrong.Yes; you should have bought day one: Nothing says day one would have done better.

questions.q: How does the catalyst side grade?
questions.story: A mega-cap followed by dozens of analysts gaps on earnings, closes strong and sets up a clean pause.
choices: B-; covered names follow through least
A+; a clean pause is all that counts
A; big names are the safest
No trade; mega-caps cannot be PEGs
questions.answer: B-; covered names follow through least
questions.why: B-. A mega-cap with many analysts gives the thinnest follow-through. Bonde: covered stocks do not do as well.
questions.lesson_line: A widely covered mega-cap is a B- cue.

wrong.A+; a clean pause is all that counts: The pause is one cue. The thin follow-through of covered names is another.
wrong.A; big names are the safest: Big names pop but follow through least.
wrong.No trade; mega-caps cannot be PEGs: A mega-cap can be a PEG; it just grades lower.

questions.q: Bought at 61.35, stop 60.21. A third sells at 67.05. How many R is that?
questions.why: 5R. Each R is the fill minus the stop, and the second third comes off at 5R. ILMN reached it from these levels.
questions.lesson_line: Count every exit in R. The second third is 5R.

questions.q: Do you buy the break?
questions.story: The market reading is Red. A leader gaps 12% on earnings on 5x volume, closes at the high, and sets up a tight pause.
choices: No; Red is mostly cash and shorts
Yes; great stocks ignore the market
Yes, at half size
Yes; Red allows an A+
questions.answer: No; Red is mostly cash and shorts
questions.why: No. In a Red market we are mostly in cash and short. Even a perfect PEG waits for the market reading to improve.
questions.lesson_line: Red market: no new PEG longs.

wrong.Yes; great stocks ignore the market: The reading is a guide for every long, leaders included.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size is for a weaker reading, not for Red.
wrong.Yes; Red allows an A+: Orange allows an A+. Red does not.

questions.q: A loss taken at the stop on a valid PEG is a mistake.
questions.why: False. A loss at the stop on a valid setup is the plan working. The scan found 31.0% reach 3R and 20.0% reach 5R before the stop.
questions.lesson_line: A loss at the stop is the system working.

questions.q: Write the plan: entry, stop, first trim.
questions.story: AMZN, 2017. A 5.5x volume gap closed at 0.92. Five flat days later it trades over the pause high of 56.14. The stop goes at 55.39.
choices: Market 56.14; stop 55.39; third at 58.39
Limit 54.00; stop 50.00; hold
Market at close; stop 56.14; 2R
Market 56.14; no stop; third at 10R
questions.why: Market 56.14, stop 55.39, a third at 58.39. One R is the fill minus the stop; three of those above the fill is 58.39. AMZN reached 3R in 13 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop and first trim, written before the open.

wrong.Limit 54.00; stop 50.00; hold: A limit far below the market never fills, and a stop that wide breaks the size rule.
wrong.Market at close; stop 56.14; 2R: A stop at the entry is no stop, and the first trim is 3R.
wrong.Market 56.14; no stop; third at 10R: A real stop goes in with the broker, and the first third is at 3R.

questions.q: What is the read?
questions.story: On day four of the pause, the stock trades back to the prior close at 11:00. It then rallies and closes above the PEG-day low.
choices: The gap filled; the setup is off
Still on; only a close ends it now
Still on, just at half size
A Gap Support; buy the close
questions.answer: The gap filled; the setup is off
questions.why: The gap filled; the setup is off. A trade at or under the prior close before a buy ends it, even if the close recovers.
questions.lesson_line: A trade back to the prior close fills the gap.

wrong.Still on; only a close ends it now: The fill test is a trade at or under the prior close, not a close.
wrong.Still on, just at half size: Half size on a dead setup is still a dead setup.
wrong.A Gap Support; buy the close: Gap Support is a later test of the gap-up low, not a fill.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought the pause break with the stop a few cents under the pause low. The next day it dips toward the stop. A friend says to move the stop down to the gap-day low to give it room.
choices: Leave it; stops only move up
Drop it to the gap-day low
Cancel it and watch it by hand
Move it half way down for room
questions.answer: Leave it; stops only move up
questions.why: Leave the stop. It only moves up. Widening it to the gap-day low after buying the pause breaks the stop rule.
questions.lesson_line: The stop never moves down or wider.

wrong.Drop it to the gap-day low: Giving it room is how a planned small loss becomes a big one.
wrong.Cancel it and watch it by hand: A real stop order sits with the broker, not in your head.
wrong.Move it half way down for room: Half way down is still wider.

questions.q: Is it a PEG?
questions.story: AMD, 2022. A stock gaps 11.2% on earnings on 2.7x volume. The day's low stays above the prior close of 116.78, but it closes at 0.23 of its range.
choices: No; a faded day, a watch at most
Yes; the gap stayed open all day
Yes; buy the close, the gap is support
No; the gap filled
questions.answer: No; a faded day, a watch at most
questions.why: No. The gap held, but the day faded to 0.23 of its range. A faded PEG day is not a PEG; it can become a delayed-reaction watch.
questions.lesson_line: A gap that fades is a watch, not a buy.

wrong.Yes; the gap stayed open all day: Holding the gap is not enough. The close matters as much.
wrong.Yes; buy the close, the gap is support: Buying a faded close is how this one lost.
wrong.No; the gap filled: The low stayed above the prior close, so the gap did not fill.

questions.q: How do you treat it?
questions.story: A stock that has run 120% in a year gaps 9% on earnings and closes at the high on huge volume.
choices: With care; it looks exhausted
An A+; strength begets strength
Buy day one at the open price
Short it; the gap is exhausted
questions.why: With care. An exhaustion gap after a huge run is not a PEG. Bonde: when everyone is excited about it, it is an exhaustion gap.
questions.lesson_line: A late gap after a huge run is a warning.

wrong.An A+; strength begets strength: A huge run into the report is a late-gap warning, not a plus.
wrong.Buy day one at the open price: We do not buy the open or after hours, and this one is late.
wrong.Short it; the gap is exhausted: A warning is not a short signal; we do not short a PEG.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought at 50.00 with the stop at 49.00. News gaps it open at 47.40, and the first 30-minute bar's low is 47.20.
choices: Get out; the loss is past 2R
Stop at 47.20 and wait
Stop at 49.00; it will bounce
Add at 47.20 to lower your cost
questions.answer: Get out; the loss is past 2R
questions.why: Get out. On a gap through the stop, the first 30-minute low is the new stop. Here that loss is past 2R, so you are out.
questions.lesson_line: Past 2R in the first half hour, get out.

wrong.Stop at 47.20 and wait: The first 30-minute low is the new stop only while the loss is within 2R.
wrong.Stop at 49.00; it will bounce: The old stop is gone, and waiting for a bounce is hope.
wrong.Add at 47.20 to lower your cost: Adding breaks one buy, one price, one stop.

questions.q: Why does the plan still work?
questions.story: Over 1,516 PEG buys in our scan of past bars, most hit the stop. Why can the plan still work?
choices: Small losses and a few big runs
A wider stop that rarely hits
A filter that lifts the win rate to 80%
Holding every winner to the next report
questions.answer: Small losses and a few big runs
questions.why: Small losses and a few big runs. In that scan 31.0% reached 3R and 20.0% reached 5R before the stop. The edge comes from the few big runs, so the trims are not pulled earlier.
questions.lesson_line: Most buys stop out. The few big runs pay for them.

wrong.A wider stop that rarely hits: Our stops stay tight; widening them is not the plan.
wrong.A filter that lifts the win rate to 80%: The scan did not find a filter that does that.
wrong.Holding every winner to the next report: Holding into a report needs 5R; the plan trims instead.

questions.q: Which day is the PEG day?
choices: The gap day, not a test weeks later
The day price tests the gap-up low
Any day above the gap-day high
The day the report is scheduled
questions.answer: The gap day, not a test weeks later
questions.why: The gap day, not a test weeks later. The gap day itself is just a PEG, never Gap Support. The later test of the gap-up low is Gap Support.
questions.lesson_line: The gap day is the PEG. The later test is Gap Support.

wrong.The day price tests the gap-up low: That later test is Gap Support.
wrong.Any day above the gap-day high: Staying above the gap-day high is not the reaction day.
wrong.The day the report is scheduled: The scheduled day is the report. The reaction day is the first regular session after it.

questions.q: Which one gets the bigger size?
questions.story: Yellow market. Gap A: 12%, 5x volume, a high close, out of a six-month base, tight pause. Gap B: up 35% in three months, mid-range close, loose pause that undercuts the low.
choices: A; B is a B- and gets less size
B; late gaps run the furthest
Both get full size; both PEGs
Neither; Yellow means all cash
questions.answer: A; B is a B- and gets less size
questions.why: A gets the bigger size. B is a B-: a late gap, a mid-range close, a loose pause. B- or lower is sized down.
questions.lesson_line: Match size to the grade. B- gets smaller size.

wrong.B; late gaps run the furthest: A late gap after a big run is a B- cue, not a plus.
wrong.Both get full size; both PEGs: The grade sets the size: A and B normal, B- or lower sized down.
wrong.Neither; Yellow means all cash: Yellow means smaller and fewer, not all cash.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, an earnings gap day is the last bar. Is the close over the 200-day? Take the pause break or pass.
choices: Pass; it is under the 200-day
Take it; the gap is very large
Take it; the close is strong
questions.why: Pass. The gap-day close was under the 200-day: a bear-market relief gap, so no long. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day, there is no long to buy.

wrong.Take it; the gap is very large: The gap is big, but size does not lift a stock over the 200-day.
wrong.Take it; the close is strong: A strong close under the 200-day is still under it.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, five sessions after an earnings gap. Is the pause holding the gap-day low? Take it or pass.
choices: Take it; the pause holds the gap
Pass; the gap has filled
Pass; the gap-day low gave way
questions.answer: Take it; the pause holds the gap
questions.why: Take it. An 8.8% gap on 5.5x volume closed at 0.92 of its range. Five flat days held the gap-day low, 1.7% deep. It broke out over the pause high.
questions.lesson_line: A gap that holds and a quiet pause are the setup.

wrong.Pass; the gap has filled: The gap is still open; price never traded back to the prior close.
wrong.Pass; the gap-day low gave way: No close sat under the gap-day low in the pause.

questions.q: A PEG day that opens up, fills the gap, then recovers into a strong close is still a valid PEG.
questions.why: False. A trade back to the prior close fills the gap, and a filled gap ends the setup. Bulkowski and ChartSchool treat a breakaway gap as one that does not fill soon.
questions.lesson_line: A gap that fills is not a PEG, whatever the close.

questions.q: May you buy it again?
questions.story: Your PEG buy was stopped out on Tuesday. By Friday the stock has formed a new pause and trades over its high.
choices: Yes; a new trigger is a new trade
No; one try per gap
Yes; double size to recover
Yes, but only after the next report
questions.answer: Yes; a new trigger is a new trade
questions.why: Yes, on a new trigger. After a stop-out we buy again only as a new trade with its own stop and every rule. At most 3 tries a week and 6 a month on one stock.
questions.lesson_line: After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger.

wrong.No; one try per gap: There is no one-try rule; there is a limit of tries a week and a month.
wrong.Yes; double size to recover: Doubling size to win it back breaks the sizing rule.
wrong.Yes, but only after the next report: Nothing says wait for the next report.

questions.q: If you do buy at 85.60 on the gap day itself, where does the stop go?
questions.story: A leader gaps up on earnings. It opens at 84.80, dips to 83.60, then climbs to 85.60.
choices: A few cents under 83.60
A few cents under the 84.80 open
At the prior close
A fixed 5% under your fill

wrong.A few cents under the 84.80 open: The open is not the day's low. The stop goes under the low so far, 83.60.
wrong.At the prior close: The prior close sits under the day's low. The stop never goes wider than under that low.
wrong.A fixed 5% under your fill: A fixed percentage ignores the chart. The stop sits under a real low.

questions.why: A few cents under 83.60, the gap day's low so far. On the gap day itself the stop goes under that low, never exactly on it.
questions.lesson_line: Day one: the stop sits a few cents under the low so far.

questions.q: Gil Morales says a buyable gap-up should hold above the intraday low of the gap-up day.
questions.why: True. The OWL Trader uses the gap-up day's intraday low as a selling guide. We put the stop a few cents under that low so far.
questions.lesson_line: The gap day's low is the line. The stop sits a few cents under it.
